clue.text: Note amounts of wood in logs

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a cord is a measured stack of cut firewood

explanation.surface: Someone notes down how much timber lies in a pile of felled trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'logs' looks like part of the timber picture, but here it is a verb: to log is to write down, as in a ship's log.
explanation.definitionFit: To log something is to write it down officially, the same sense as noting it in a register.

clue.text: Certain soldiers gave up — retreated

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
ceded means surrendered or gave up territory

explanation.surface: Some troops surrendered and withdrew from the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Receded means drew back or moved away, like a tide going out.

clue.text: Fletcher, a man of the church

explanation.surface: An arrow-maker is described as a religious man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian led the mutiny on the Bounty; a follower of Christ is likewise a churchman by that name.

clue.text: The relationship arrived at in a foreign port

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romance struck up once someone reached an overseas harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrived' is only a link here. 'relationship' suggests romance, but the sense is mathematical: the proportion between two quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the proportion between two amounts, how one stands to another.

clue.text: Tired fellow coming to a standstill

parts.note: stale means tired or worn out, as an overworked athlete goes stale
a mate is a companion or fellow

explanation.surface: An exhausted man finally grinds to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock where neither side can move, borrowed from chess.

clue.text: Business award added with order

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry award
and is the word for addition, as in two and two

explanation.surface: A firm wins a prize together with a contract for goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An order and a command are both instructions given with authority.

clue.text: A blow for many an awkward person

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a common crossword sense of many
a lout is a clumsy, uncouth fellow

explanation.surface: A punch that is meant for a crowd of oafs.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy hit or cuff with the hand.

clue.text: The late spring blossom transported people!

explanation.surface: Flowers at the end of spring are said to send people into raptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' suggests ecstasy, but it means carried by sea: the ship that took the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn blossom flowering in May comes late in spring; the ship of that name carried the Pilgrims across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Anonymous fabric available in the market place

indicators.note: anonymous means without a name, and N stands for name, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: angora is a soft fabric made from rabbit or goat hair

explanation.surface: Unlabelled cloth can be bought at the bazaar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anonymous' looks like a description of the fabric, but it means 'nameless': drop N (name) from ANGORA.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the open public square of an ancient Greek city, used for trade and assembly.

clue.text: Reject rendered without blemish

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to render a song is to perform it, so rendered means did
a scar is a mark or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Something is turned down because it came out flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old sense of 'outside', so the first piece wraps around the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard is to throw away or cast aside as unwanted.

clue.text: The gold standard

parts.note: the phrase usually means a benchmark of excellence or a monetary system, but read literally it asks for the unit by which the purity of gold is measured

explanation.walkthrough: The financial or 'best of its kind' sense is the bait; the literal sense, the scale on which gold is graded (24 being pure), gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold purity is expressed in these units, 24 of them meaning the metal is pure.

clue.text: Article on mousy characters — not named

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of the word mousy are taken and reordered

explanation.surface: A timid little piece of writing is published without a byline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people in a story but means letters: the anagram of 'mousy' gives YMOUS to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anonymous has no name attached, like an unsigned letter.

clue.text: Unreliable but attractive girl 'with love nest

parts.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fickle beauty sets up a cosy home for romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest person cannot be trusted, so the word is a near synonym for untrustworthy.

clue.text: Experiences in the French capital

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
to have, as in having a good time, is to experience; has is its third-person form

explanation.surface: A traveller has various adventures in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'French capital' a phrase meaning Paris, but 'the French' gives LA and 'capital' alone is the definition: the capital of Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet.

clue.text: Verdi's extraordinary energy

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of its ordinary order, so the letters of the composer's name are jumbled

parts.note: the composer's name; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Praise for the Italian opera composer's remarkable vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' reads as praise for the composer, but it signals that VERDI is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means vigour or push, the energy to get things done.

clue.text: Get rams in perhaps — these are getting out

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged some other way, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: A farmer is told to bring the sheep in, while others are leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals a rearrangement of GET RAMS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: People leaving their home country to settle abroad are emigrants.

clue.text: The ending of a quarrel

parts.note: a quarrel is also the square-headed bolt fired from a crossbow, and its ending is the pointed tip that strikes

explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is a peace-making end to an argument; the archery sense of 'quarrel', a crossbow bolt, gives the real meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip at the front of a missile from a bow is its head.

clue.text: Go off a schedule, but may be brought round

parts.note: food that goes off will rot
a table is a timetable or schedule

explanation.surface: Drifting from a timetable, though one might be persuaded back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' suggests persuading someone, but it means turned round, like a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be spun or turned on an axis is able to be rotated.

clue.text: The promptitude of an aristocrat in letter writing

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
the letter S written out as a word is ess

explanation.surface: A nobleman shows quickness when answering correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter writing' suggests correspondence, but it is the letter S written as a word, ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Promptitude is promptness, being early or on time.

clue.text: Volume incorporating one new landmass

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body of something, so the second part sits inside the first

parts.note: content can mean capacity or volume, as in the cubic content of a tank
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A book includes a fresh chapter about a vast territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is one of the great land areas of the globe, such as Africa or Asia.

clue.text: Keep misusing dialect

indicators.note: misusing a word implies handling it wrongly, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to a broken regional speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is a noun here, the stronghold of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, a fortress or stronghold.

clue.text: Bishop protecting a king is comparatively unusual

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so these letters go around the next piece

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A chess position where a bishop guards a king, which seldom happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is misleading: no piece on the board is meant. RR (Right Reverend) is the standard crossword bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer is the comparative of rare, describing something seen less often than another.

clue.text: To retire would appear the right way out

parts.note: an egress is an exit or way out

explanation.surface: Leaving work seems the proper exit route.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to go back or withdraw, a sense of retiring as in retreating.

clue.text: Thin, and so light

explanation.surface: Someone says a thing is slender and therefore weighs little.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to grow thinner towards one end; a taper is also a slender wax candle, giving light.

clue.text: A Turkish dignitary remains lying in state

indicators.note: lying in places one thing inside another

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: An Ottoman official's body lies in state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying in state' suggests a funeral, but 'state' here is an American state's postal code, and 'lying in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman officer or governor.

clue.text: Coming to and bearing with everyone involved

indicators.note: to be involved is to be wrapped up within, so these letters are placed inside the other word

parts.note: toting means carrying or bearing a load
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A party arrives, carrying luggage, with the whole group taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to' sounds like waking up but means amounting to, as a bill totals a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill amounting to ten pounds is adding up to that sum; the same idea as reaching a sum.

clue.text: A point to be observed in the South or North

indicators.note: the answer can be seen within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A compass bearing that can be spotted whether you head south or north.
explanation.walkthrough: It is concealed across 'SouTH OR North'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a stem, a natural point.

clue.text: Catch Sarah up — just like that!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Sal is a pet name for Sarah
so means in that way, as in 'do it so'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to grab a girl and lift her, exactly as shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a noosed rope used to catch cattle.

clue.text: Get up late

parts.note: it reads as oversleeping, but 'late' means deceased and 'get up' means raise, so it is about raising the dead from a grave

explanation.walkthrough: The lie-in reading is the trap: 'the late' is a polite term for the dead, and the getting up is digging them out of their tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to remove a body from its burial place, which is lifting up one who has died.

clue.text: Viewed, so it's said, as disagreement

indicators.note: the phrase signals a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: something viewed has been seen

explanation.surface: A remark that something has been watched, described as a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a scene is a public row or angry display, a disagreement out loud.

clue.text: Oils in a compound relationship.

indicators.note: to compound is to mix things together, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Oils combine in a chemical mixture that binds them together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a chemistry noun but is the anagram signal: OILS IN A reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a connection or close association, sometimes a secret affair.

clue.text: One is the number they think of

definitions.text: One is the number they think of

parts.words: One is the number they think of
parts.note: people who think only of number one, that is themselves, are selfish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a party guessing game; 'number one' is slang for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred people care chiefly about themselves, putting number one first.
